content:
I am working on a sequence of PRs (containing #36989, where the problem first shows up) whose ultimate goal is to have a proof of the Mordell-Weil Theorem for elliptic curves over number fields in Mathlib. This needs to import analysis (via heights) and algebraic geometry (for the elliptic curves). However:

Warning: Modules starting with Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry are not allowed to import modules starting with Mathlib.Analysis.
Warning: Modules starting with Mathlib.NumberTheory are not allowed to import modules starting with Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.

So this seems to be impossible within the existing folder structure.

Is this the time to set up a new top-level folder Mathlib.ArithmeticGeometry (where we are allowed to import everything we might need)?
Or should we add exceptions to the current rules?
Adding exceptions is fine (e.g., this is what I did for L-functions).
See this message: #mathlib4 > AkraBazzi not allowed to import measure theory @ 💬
Was this for L-functions attached to elliptic curves? If so maybe it would make sense to make the new folder and move the L-function stuff there.
Well, L-functions of elliptic curves aren't in mathlib yet. The machinery to construct them are still being PRed.

I would expect the arithmetic geometry material to grow considerably over time, so without establishing a separate place for it, we'll likely have to keep adding exceptions. So I would like to argue for Mathlib.ArithmeticGeometry as a more long-term stable solution.

This was recently discussed here: #mathlib4 > Algebraic geometry import linter. The conclusion was adding an exception to Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites, but I would think that the theory of heights should not go there.

So how about adding a new folder Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Heights and add exceptions for that?
An additional top level folder causes quite a bit of additional overhead and it will constantly raise the question of where things should go (What counts as arithmetic geometry? What is basic algebraic geometry?). In contrast to this, it is reasonly well-defined what should go into the folder AlgebraicGeometry.Heights.
How about ArithmeticGeometry is anything that imports both NumberTheory and AlgebraicGeometry?
An ArithmeticGeometry folder looks fine to me. And it should be allowed to import anything

To reiterate my point from the other thread:

Also, having both AlgebraicGeometry and ArithmeticGeometry as top level folders could be confusing for newcomers.

On top of this, we would have to maintain an additional topic label, new label dependencies, new reviewers interests, more maintainer merge channels for very little gain. I would expect that all t-algebraic-geometry reviewers would also be t-arithmetic-geometry reviewers and vice versa (except if the split is along the EllipticCurve vs Scheme-theory division, which I don't think is the proposal?).
A compromise, which I also proposed in the other thread, could be to add an Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.ArithmeticGeometry subfolder with relaxed import restrictions.

It's hard for me to argue that "heights" are "arithmetic geometry". How about a top level folder Arithmetic? This word has a technical meaning (it's not just 2+2=4), e.g. Serre's book "A course in arithmetic" which develops the theory of quadratic forms, L-functions and modular forms.
Is a subfolder of the number theory folder a possible home? (to avoid the pain of creating a new top level folder that @Christian Merten mentions)
Wont we eventually need an arithmetic geometry folder anyways?
What would be the scope of this folder? How would it relate to AlgebraicGeometry and which (groups of) people would you expect to have this new folder in their reviewers interests?
We put all the things from this article in it
I think the “pain of a new top level folder” is exaggerated. This is something we want eventually and there is no point trying to avoid it. (I’m not commenting on whether heights belong there or not)
I am not yet convinced by the statement that we eventually want such a folder.
So your preferred solution is to put heights in number theory and add an exception to the import rules? I could definitely argue that heights were number theory!

Warning: Modules starting with Mathlib.NumberTheory are not allowed to import modules starting with Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.

I'm late to the party here, but: I think this linter is a really bad idea, and needs to go.

Number theory has a reputation as the magpie of mathematics :crow:, casually borrowing ideas from absolutely every other branch. Many major developments in algebraic geometry (e.g. schemes, etale cohomology) were partly or wholly motivated by number-theoretic applications; and current work in algebraic number theory is absolutely inseparable from algebraic geometry.
I don't see why number theory should have any import restrictions. I thought the point of developing anything in mathlib is to use them in number theory.

Kevin Buzzard said:

It's hard for me to argue that "heights" are "arithmetic geometry"

Kevin Buzzard said:

I could definitely argue that heights were number theory!

Many applications of heights are in arithmetic geometry (not all, certainly), and you can define (and use) heights also for general function fields, so "number theory", in a sense, is also too narrow.

But I'm fine with basically all proposed solutions (new top-level folder (whatever its name), new folder under NumberTheory, new folder under AlgebraicGeometry).
I am inclined to put arithmetic geometry as a subfolder of number theory and the Mathematics Subject Classification(MSC2020) seem to agree.
But heights in particular appear as both 11G50 (number theory) and 14G40 (algebraic geometry)!

I don't really care whether it's in NumberTheory or AlgebraicGeometry or ArithmeticGeometry, but all I ask for is that the material on heights on elliptic curves should be in (?).EllipticCurve.(Number/Global)Field.Heights. I'd be happy to move the entire folder into NumberTheory if necessary.

So maybe the way to proceed for now is

  • to lift the import restriction(s) on NumberTheory, and
  • to have the material somewhere in the NumberTheory folder.

The potential addition of a new top-level ArithmeticGeometry can be discussed again at a later point when more relevant material is there.
I get the argument that the stuff in there has nothing to do with number theory at the moment, but it has nothing to do with algebraic geometry either
Waiting for more relevant material is fine, but I note that when Condensed became a thing it had like 2 files, so we should start somewhere
If everything related to elliptic curves should be together, it currently cannot go into AlgebraicGeometry. I assume a top-level EllipticCurve folder will not be met with a lot of enthusiasm...
Yeah, but a top-level ArithmeticGeometry folder will be :)
Anyways I propose moving everything to NumberTheory
What I would like to avoid is the PRs becoming blocked because of this discusssion.

Sometimes I don't even think number theory is the study of numbers any more; it's just the study of things that people who consider themselves number theorists care about, and seems like number theorists care about everything
(This reminds me of a definition of "combinatorics" I've read in a book: combinatorics is what combinatorialists do.)
I think the current import restriction on Algebraic geometry is also somewhat weird. Results about complex algebraic variety definitely belongs there but we definitely need analysis for them.
I guess for now we'll just disable the thing that disables module imports into number theory, and I'll make a PR that moves everything into NumberTheory
#37224 allows NumberTheory to import AlgebraicGeometry. (I think it makes sense to deal with this separately.)
